summary: Google's own numbers are in for the first time: clicks from people who didn't search for Meridian by name rose to 151 in the last 28 days, up from 131.
The quickest win is the sports injury page: Google showed it 223 times for “sports injury treatment” but nobody clicked. The sciatica page sits just off Google's first page.
Nothing from the list was published this week. The pregnancy back pain page is still estimated #1, but Google shows that search is small (16 appearances in 28 days).

topActions.text: Approve #40 and click Ship it. Claude rewrites the sports injury page's Google title and description so people searching “sports injury treatment” click through.
Approve #41 and click Ship it. Claude sharpens the sciatica page's title and headings and links to it from related pages, to reach Google's first page.
Approve the ACC page (#25) and click Ship it. Claude drafts it, then Nina checks the ACC wording before it goes live.

tldr: Google data (Search Console, last 28 days to 21 Sep vs the 28 days before): 267 clicks (269 before) from 4,155 appearances in Google (4,148). Clicks from people not searching for Meridian by name rose from 131 to 151, while name searches fell (“meridian osteopathy” 71 clicks, down from 115), so the total stayed flat. 32 searches now show Meridian on Google's first page, up from 27. “Osteopath christchurch” improved from an average position of 9.9 to 6.2 (166 appearances, 6 clicks). The fertility acupuncture page is the clearest success: position 2.8 for “fertility acupuncture christchurch” with 8 clicks, up from 5.6 and 3 clicks. The core update that finished on 21 Sep may still be moving numbers, so read small changes cautiously.

Estimated ranks (a US-based web search, not what someone in Christchurch sees): 30 searches checked. The pregnancy back pain page held #1 and is also #1 for “back pain during pregnancy christchurch”. The sports injury page dropped out of the estimated top 10 again (was #4). Better Health now has a dedicated postnatal page ranking #1 for “postnatal osteopath christchurch”, so the postpartum idea (#36) faces more competition than before. Estimated ranks and Google's figures disagree for “acupuncture christchurch” (estimated absent, Google says 8.7), which is a reminder to trust Search Console first.

Pool changes: added “sports injury treatment” and “sciatica treatment christchurch” from Search Console, and “is acupuncture covered by acc” and “osteopath christchurch price” from Google's autocomplete, which worked again after six blocked runs. Dropped four low-signal searches. New items #40–#42 all come straight from Search Console: searches where Meridian already appears but gets few or no clicks. Nothing from the list shipped since 18 Sep; the only site change was switching off the June practitioner spotlight.

gaps.title: No ACC landing page
gaps.why: Neck-pain and back-pain condition pages ship (items #22, #23 closed). The remaining piece of G7 is a single indexable /acc/ URL. **URGENT COMPETITIVE MOVEMENT 2026-09-18**: betterhealthosteopathy.nz/acc/ now holds #2 on 'osteopath acc christchurch' — Better Health has just shipped a dedicated ACC landing page, which is exactly what Meridian's item #25 proposes. Active Health still holds #1 on the query with their own /christchurch/osteopathy/ page's ACC-registered messaging. This means the competitive window for #25 is closing rapidly — a Meridian /acc/ URL shipped in the next 4-6 weeks slots in behind two entrenched competitors; delayed further, it faces a third. Item #25 covers, and the copy angle needs to match PR #113's site-wide reframing from 'we lodge claims for you' to 'ACC-registered provider' framing (Google Ads classifier reads the old wording as paid-intermediary facilitation).

gaps.title: No blog / editorial content
gaps.why: Freshness cliff at ~3 months. Confirmed again 2026-09-18: content depth + freshness remain the dominant differentiator against blog-post-heavy competitors like osteopath-christchurch.com (headaches / migraine / cranial / baby / arthritis), MK Osteopathy (TMJ), headachetendon.nz (chiropractor, though its 3+ week #1 on 'lower back pain christchurch' was DISPLACED this run by Better Health), and triskelionconcussioncare.co.nz's cross-body-region expansion into arthritis / back-pain / neck-pain / concussion via dedicated landing URLs. Meridian's Practitioner Spotlight infrastructure (PR #108) is the closest thing we have to blog cadence — one entry per month, homepage-surface only, not a separate URL. Item #14 covers the full blog build. **STRONGEST-EVER EVIDENCE 2026-09-18**: Meridian's /conditions/pregnancy-back-pain/ reached **#1** on 'pregnancy back pain christchurch' this run — the FIRST TIME any Meridian URL has ever held #1 on a tracked query. This proves definitively that dedicated, indexable, schema-marked condition URLs with citation-ready intros (#31) and structured list blocks (#34) can reach the very top in this market, not just top-10. Combined with the sports-injury-recovery URL's return to #4 the same week, the URL-per-condition thesis is validated across two pages and multiple SERP positions (#1, #4, #5, #6, #9). Item #14 (blog collection built on the same infrastructure) is the highest-leverage path to more ranked URLs and remains **Tier 1**. Cloudflare's 15 Sep AI-crawler default further raises the leverage of owned Q&A content (ad-supported publishers being shut out of AI training crawlers means models will lean harder on primary-source clinic sites).

gaps.title: No off-site citation strategy
gaps.why: Reddit is a major AI-citation source but the platform mix shifted sharply in the Jul-Aug window. UNCHANGED 2026-09-18: no material movement in the Reddit-Perplexity litigation / licensing situation since 31 Jul motion-to-dismiss rejection. Between Jul 1 and Aug 19, 2026, Perplexity supplied 71% of tracked Reddit citations while ChatGPT supplied 23%; ChatGPT Search citations linking to Reddit fell from ~250/day in early Aug to 16/day the week after Aug 14 — a -94% decline in six days. Reddit's Perplexity share is now ~24%, Gemini 0.1%. Item #15 stays on the backlog scoped to Perplexity-visibility only (larger share, smaller more curated source pool means single well-structured posts can surface); skip the ChatGPT-oriented seeding. 90/10 rule still applies: 90% non-promotional, 2–4 weeks of karma-building before any mention of Meridian.

items.title: Add speakable blocks on service intros
items.why: Unlikely to move your rankings. Google has kept this feature in test mode for years, and a large 2026 study found that adding this kind of behind-the-scenes code gave no real lift. It's cheap, but a good one to dismiss.
items.body: Wrap the short answer at the top of each service page in “speakable” code, which marks the text a voice assistant should read aloud. Google has kept speakable in test mode for years, and a 2026 study of 1,885 pages found that adding this kind of behind-the-scenes code made no clear difference to AI or search visibility. The best predictor of being quoted by AI is ranking well in normal Google results. Cheap to do, but low value; a reasonable one to dismiss.

items.title: Auto-fetch Google Business Profile reviews at build time
items.why: Up-to-date review numbers on your own site help visitors trust you, but they don't change your Google ranking by themselves. Getting new Google reviews (#16) is what moves rankings. It also needs a paid Google Places key set up first.
items.body: Pull the Google review count and star rating into the site at build time, so the numbers on the site stay current without manual edits. Needs a Google Places API key (a paid Google Cloud account) set up by the clinic first. Fresh reviews matter a lot for Google Maps rankings, but showing the count on the website doesn't change rankings by itself; getting new reviews (#16) does. Pairs well with #16 once reviews are flowing.

items.title: Start a blog (2 posts/month)
items.reviewer: the practitioner who writes each post
items.why: Nearby clinics that rank for specific conditions mostly do it with one helpful article per condition. Your own pages back this up: the fertility acupuncture page now sits at position 2.8 in Google with 8 clicks a month. It's the biggest job on the list, and every post needs a practitioner.
files: PR #108 Practitioner Spotlight infra can be extended rather than a from-scratch build
items.body: Short, practical articles, one per condition or question, each with the practitioner's name, publish and update dates, and 3–5 common questions. Competitors like osteopath-christchurch.com and Better Health rank on many condition searches this way. Meridian's evidence: the fertility page (position 2.8, 8 clicks in 28 days, up from 3) and the pregnancy back pain page (estimated #1, though only 16 Google appearances a month) show dedicated pages work here. Start with topics people already search for, using Search Console's query list, rather than guessing. The practitioner spotlight setup can be reused for the page layout and CMS. Two posts a month is enough if each is genuinely useful.

items.title: Answer local Reddit questions to show up in Perplexity AI search
items.why: Reddit mentions mainly help with the Perplexity AI search tool, which few NZ patients use. Time-consuming and hard to measure, so low priority.
items.body: Genuine, helpful answers in NZ Reddit threads (r/chch, r/newzealand) about osteopathy, ACC and back pain, with very occasional mentions of Meridian after weeks of ordinary participation. This mainly helps with Perplexity, an AI search tool few NZ patients use; ChatGPT cites Reddit much less since August. Time-consuming and hard to measure, so low priority.

items.title: Ask happy patients for Google reviews and reply to every review within 48 hours
items.why: Regular new Google reviews, answered within a day or two, are one of the best-proven ways for a local clinic to rank higher in Google Maps results.
items.body: Send a short email after each appointment asking happy patients for a Google review, using the email system the site already has. Reply to every review within a day or two, naming the practitioner or treatment the reviewer mentioned rather than using a template. Recent reviews carry the most weight in Google Maps rankings (Whitespark's 2026 study rates review recency as the top individual local factor), and Google's AI answers also draw on review text. Aim for about one new review a week.

items.title: Build an ACC page: Active Health and Better Health already have one
items.why: People search for ACC osteopaths, and Better Health and The House of Acupuncture both have dedicated ACC pages. Meridian doesn't appear for these searches at all yet. ACC wording is sensitive (see July's rewording), so Nina should check it.
items.body: A single page at /acc/ explaining ACC for patients. Estimated ranks for “osteopath acc christchurch” are unchanged: Active Health #1 and Better Health's ACC page #2. For acupuncture, The House of Acupuncture has a dedicated ACC page, and Google's autocomplete suggests “is acupuncture covered by acc”. The page should say that Meridian is an ACC-registered provider (osteopathy with Nina Hu, acupuncture with Min Jin), what a patient pays, that no referral is needed, and that Meridian isn't part of ACC, with a link to acc.co.nz. Don't describe filing claims on the patient's behalf (see the July Google Ads rewording). Lead with a short 40–60 word answer, as on the condition pages.

items.title: Add a concussion page (only if someone at Meridian treats concussion)
items.why: Check first: none of your practitioners lists concussion as a special interest. Only build this page if someone at Meridian treats concussion and is happy to be named on it. Otherwise, dismiss it.
items.body: A /conditions/concussion/ page built like the existing condition pages. Estimated ranks for “concussion osteopath christchurch”: osteo.co.nz #1, Better Health #2 (through an associate osteopath's profile) and Triskelion Concussion Care #3. Meridian isn't visible, and Search Console shows no concussion searches reaching the site. Post-concussion symptoms (headaches, dizziness, neck pain) overlap with conditions Meridian already treats, but no practitioner lists concussion as a special interest. Confirm someone treats it and is happy to be named before building.

items.title: Check Google's AI Overviews report in Search Console and save a baseline
items.why: Search Console is now connected to this dashboard. The remaining step is a 5-minute look at Google's AI report, so you can later tell whether new pages show up in AI answers.
items.body: Search Console is connected and feeding this dashboard. Its separate AI report (appearances in AI Overviews and AI Mode) isn't pulled in automatically. In Search Console, open Performance, pick the AI features view, set the date range to the last 3 months, and save a screenshot as the “before” picture ahead of any new pages. The report shows appearances only, not clicks. Google's core update finished on 21 Sep and a spam update started on 24 Sep, so give it until mid-October before reading much into changes. No website changes needed.

items.title: Add a postpartum recovery page (Kaylee)
items.why: Kaylee lists pregnancy and postpartum care as a special interest, but Better Health now has a dedicated postnatal page ranking #1 (estimated), so this is no longer the easy gap it looked like. Search Console shows no postpartum searches reaching the site yet.
items.body: A separate /conditions/postpartum-recovery/ page, built like the existing condition pages, so the pregnancy back pain page (estimated #1) keeps its focus. For the last three weeks “postpartum osteopath christchurch” returned very few results. This week Better Health's new /care/postnatal/ page is #1 for “postnatal osteopath christchurch”, and Triskelion and Active Health also appear. Still worth doing if Kaylee wants to lead it, since the pregnancy page shows this pattern can rank, but expect a harder climb. Add it to the homepage conditions grid.

items.title: Get clicks for “sports injury treatment”: shown 223 times, no clicks
items.why: Google already shows your sports injury page for “sports injury treatment” (223 times in 28 days, average position 8.7) but nobody clicked. A clearer Google title and description is the cheapest way to turn those appearances into visits.
items.body: The page's Google title is currently “Sports Injury Recovery | Meridian Osteopathy”, which doesn't match what people type. Change it to lead with “Sports Injury Treatment in Christchurch”, and rewrite the description to say who it's for and what happens at a first visit, in plain words, keeping “no referral needed” and ACC-registered status. Match the main heading to the new title. Related Search Console searches: “sports injury treatments” (11.4), “sports recovery” (11.3), “sport injuries rehabilitation” (13.8). No clinical claims change, so no practitioner review is needed.

items.title: Move the sciatica page onto Google's first page for “sciatica treatment”
items.why: The sciatica page is Meridian's most-shown condition page (272 appearances in 28 days) but sits at position 16.5 for “sciatica treatment”, just off the first page. It's already position 5 for “sciatica treatment christchurch”.
items.body: Appearances grew from 187 to 272 but clicks are only 2. Change the Google title to “Sciatica Treatment in Christchurch | Meridian Osteopathy” and make the main heading say “Sciatica treatment”. Add clear links to the sciatica page from the back pain page and the homepage conditions section using the words “sciatica treatment”. Search Console also shows “osteopath for sciatica” (8.8), “can osteopath help with sciatica” (9) and “sciatica specialist” (11.2). Wording and links only; if new clinical content is added, ask a practitioner to check it.

items.title: Make the acupuncture page, not the homepage, the one Google shows for acupuncture
items.why: “Acupuncture christchurch” is your biggest non-name search (291 appearances), but Google shows the homepage at position 8.7 and clicks fell from 9 to 4. The acupuncture page itself sits at position 4.3 for the searches it does get.
items.body: When Google picks the homepage for a service search, the result is less specific and tends to get fewer clicks. Lead the acupuncture page's Google title with “Acupuncture & Dry Needling in Christchurch”, shorten its description (currently long and cut off), and link to it from the homepage with the words “acupuncture in Christchurch”. The same applies to “dry needling christchurch” (62 appearances, position 10.4, homepage shown). Experimental because Google may keep preferring the homepage; check Search Console four weeks after shipping.
